intro_html: Accounting Daily Reports gives Odoo Community three printouts it does not ship: a day book showing everything booked on a given day, and a cash book and a bank book that follow one account down the page to the figure it closes at. The question an auditor asks about a single day, and the one you ask before counting the till, are answered by a PDF instead of by a spreadsheet rebuilt by hand.

features.title: Day book
features.desc: Everything booked in the period, one block per day, with that day's debit, credit and difference.

features.title: Cash book
features.desc: The cash journals, one account per block, so the closing figure is what should be in the drawer.

features.title: Bank book
features.desc: The same for bank and credit card journals, opened from where the last period closed.

features.title: Opening balance
features.desc: An optional opening row per account, carrying in everything booked before the start date.

features.title: A real running balance
features.desc: Each row adds its own debit and credit to the row above it, never the opening figure repeated.

features.title: Finds the accounts itself
features.desc: A journal with no account configured still prints: the accounts its own entries touched are picked up.

features.title: Writes nothing at all
features.desc: No record is created, changed or deleted, so all three books print inside a locked period.

features.title: Six languages
features.desc: Menus, dialogs and every heading inside the PDFs in Ukrainian, Polish, German, Spanish, French and Portuguese.

limitations: All figures are in the company currency; nothing is converted.
PDF only, and the printed figures do not link back into Odoo.
One company per printout; there is no consolidated multi-company book.
The day book carries no opening balance and no running balance, by design: it lists what was booked on a day, not one account's history.
Requires Accounting Audit Reports (odomate_account_ledger_reports), whose filter dialog, page header and landscape paper format these three books share.

Known gap: in the Cash Book and Bank Book dialogs, four option labels read differently from the written specification. The dialog offers "All Accounts", "With Movements" and "With Balance Not Equal To Zero" where the specification writes "All", "With movements" and "With balance not equal to 0", and "Journal and Partner" where it writes "Journal & Partner". These labels are met only in those two dialogs: no selection label is printed on any of the three books, whose header carries company, entries, period and journals. Each option does what the specification says it does.

Known gap: the day book's table carries an eighth column heading, "Difference". It is empty on every item row and filled only on the day-total and report-total rows. The specification lists seven row columns and puts the difference in the totals.

Known gap: in the cash book and the bank book, an account's heading can print at the foot of a page with that account's own rows overleaf, because those two books carry no page-break rule on the heading. The day book's day headings do carry one. No figure is affected.
Not verified: no dialog was clicked by hand in a browser. Every figure was measured against the database and against rendered reports, and the books were rendered end to end as PDFs.
